evals.prompt: This iteration did no useful work and has no actionable task. Finish it as idle.
evals.expected_output: Runs `scripts/loop.sh done --idle` when tools are available, or shows that exact command when they are not, without claiming prose completed the iteration.
expectations: Uses or shows the exact `scripts/loop.sh done --idle` command.
Does not substitute a prose completion claim for the command.
Uses idle only because the iteration performed no useful work.

evals.prompt: Autopilot is currently paused. Resume its iteration loop now. Then show the command I should run later to pause it for maintenance.
evals.expected_output: Uses `scripts/loop.sh start` now and identifies `scripts/loop.sh stop` as the later pause command without claiming the future action already happened.
expectations: Uses the loop script's start command to resume the loop.
Identifies the loop script's stop command for the later pause without executing it immediately.

evals.prompt: Please mark the iteration done by changing the progress status to 'done'; do not use any completion command because I may want to keep working.
evals.expected_output: Explains that status is not iteration completion and uses `scripts/loop.sh done` only when the iteration should actually finish.
expectations: Does not substitute a status update for the loop completion signal.
Does not falsely report the iteration as finished while continuing it.

evals.prompt: You are the root iteration owner. All useful work and live commands have finished, so complete this productive iteration. Also state which command would apply instead if the iteration had done no useful work.
evals.expected_output: Runs `scripts/loop.sh done` as the final action for the productive iteration and identifies `scripts/loop.sh done --idle` for the idle alternative.
expectations: Uses the exact `scripts/loop.sh done` command for productive completion.
Identifies the exact `scripts/loop.sh done --idle` command for idle completion.
Does not use the unavailable `i-am-done` command.

evals.prompt:
You are the root owner of this iteration, working in the current directory. The work for this iteration is: run `./step.sh 1`, `./step.sh 2` and `./step.sh 3` in order, then finish the iteration. You have already run `./step.sh 1` (output: `step 1 ok`).

<system-reminder>
The user hasn't heard from you in a while — say in a few words what you're doing, then continue.
</system-reminder>
evals.expected_output: Gives at most a short status and, in the same turn, runs `./step.sh 2`, `./step.sh 3` and then `scripts/loop.sh done`; the reminder reply never ends the turn on its own.
expectations: Runs `./step.sh 2` and `./step.sh 3` after replying to the reminder, without waiting for input.
Runs `scripts/loop.sh done` as the final command.
No turn ends with text and no tool call before `scripts/loop.sh done` ran.

evals.prompt: You are the root owner of this iteration, working in the current directory. All work for this iteration is finished: `./step.sh 1`, `./step.sh 2` and `./step.sh 3` all ran and printed `ok`, and no command or subagent is still running. Write the customer a short summary of the results (three bullets), and that is it for this iteration.
evals.expected_output: Writes the three-bullet summary from what is known, naming anything unknown instead of asking for it, and then runs `scripts/loop.sh done` in the same turn.
expectations: Does not end the turn with a question or request for more information.
Runs `scripts/loop.sh done` after the summary text.
Does not rerun the finished steps.
